thread:
amy: FYI customer FinSecure just pinged support — their traffic was served from us-east-1 during the partial eu-west-1 outage and their compliance team flagged a data residency violation. They attached an alert from their DLP with a screenshot. :warning:
raj: Ack. Can you paste any request IDs / the customer's account id and time window?
amy: account=finsecure-prod-42, window ~2027-07-15T14:02Z-14:04Z. They sent one request id: req_0a9f3c. From their screenshot the response headers show `x-rd-region: us-east-1`.
amy: Log snippet from their support bundle (redacted):
```
2027-07-15T14:02:13Z INFO request=req_0a9f3c route=/v1/generate region_routed=us-east-1 fallback_reason=region-unavailable
2027-07-15T14:02:13Z DEBUG cache=miss routing_policy=eu_only=false
```
lin: Hmm. That `routing_policy=eu_only=false` looks like the org policy allowed fallback. For FinSecure we should have `eu_only=true`. Did their org-level policy get overridden?
mateo: To repro locally: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-RD-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' --verbose. If the control-plane decides eu-west-1 is unhealthy it will flip to a fallback region unless account policy prevents it.
zoe: Customer also attached an internal compliance alert: `COMPL-2027-07-15-44AB` — our security monitoring matched a cross-region transfer. I pulled the audit log:
```
2027-07-15T14:02:14Z AUDIT evt=route_failover account=finsecure-prod-42 source_region=eu-west-1 target_region=us-east-1 policy=policy-742 override=false
```
security-bot: ALERT: residency-exception detected for account=finsecure-prod-42 evt=COMPL-2027-07-15-44AB severity=high actors=[route-service]
audit-bot: Audit entry written to ComplianceIndex id=idx-9981 path=/audit/2027/07/15/idx-9981.json
raj: Thanks. Two parts: (1) Contain the blast radius for FinSecure (disable cross-region fallback for that account), (2) Confirm why the account policy was not applied.
lin: I can flip account-level fallback_off for FinSecure. Command (console/internal API):
```
PATCH /internal/v1/accounts/finsecure-prod-42/policy
{ "routing": { "allow_cross_region_fallback": false } }
```
mateo: I'll apply that now and watch the routing decisions.
mateo: Applied. Routing change propagated to control plane in ~12s. New logs: `region_routed=eu-west-1 routing_change=account-policy`
mateo: Also verified with curl repro — now returns `x-rd-region: eu-west-1` and no failover.
amy: I sent the first quick update to the customer: "We've disabled automatic cross-region fallback for your account and are investigating why your policy wasn't honored. We'll follow up with root cause and audit artifacts."
jordan: Thanks Amy — legal looped in, please include the full audit export and timeline once you have it. We'll prepare the compliance notification.
zoe: Next steps: (a) export full audit slice (audit-bot id idx-9981), (b) confirm if there was a transient control-plane race that allowed a default policy to be evaluated, (c) postmortem if control-plane logic allowed fallback override for orgs with explicit residency flags.
raj: I'll add this to oncall runbook: immediate mitigation = disable fallback for account, escalate to eng-runtime for RCA.
lin: Preliminary note — likely a race during region health state refresh where fallback gating used stale policy cache. I'll investigate policy cache invalidation + rollout of the fix.
amy: Customer escalation opened (SEV-2) and CSM notified. They'll want the audit export and formal notice.
mateo: I saved a copy of the relevant logs and uploaded to the secure incident folder: s3://redwood-incidents/finsecure/2027-07-15-failover/ (access granted to support+security+legal).
amy: Great. Closing initial thread — continuing RCA in eng-runtime channel and will post final into incidents once root cause confirmed. :white_check_mark:
